opposite_world_test.explanation: Two-tier verdict. TIER 1 (rigid, cannot flip): 'the dephasing fixed points are exactly the states diagonal in the chosen basis' is a one-line linear-algebra theorem (Pi_i Pi_j = delta_ij Pi_i); SBT could NOT have 'retrodicted' off-diagonal or non-orthogonal fixed points, nor non-idempotent collapse. TIER 2 (fully flexible, the real ad-hocness locus): WHICH basis is 'the' pointer/record basis is a free, undetermined input (missing_interfaces l.102; l.856 'No selection rule derived'). Given any orthonormal basis B, SBT declares B 'the record basis' and 'recovers' the B-diagonal states as classical objects with identical machinery. So 'nature's classical pointer states are diagonal in basis B-prime, not B' is accommodated with zero strain by relabeling f. SBT predicts NOTHING about which basis nature picks (einselection, which it disclaims). It also cannot certify multiplicity from idempotence alone (constant-map guardrail D-IC-02), so a degenerate 'one object' world is equally consistent unless dim>=2 is assumed. Net: the FORM of the answer is theorem-rigid, but the empirically load-bearing content (preferred basis, Born weights, single outcome) is exactly the part SBT leaves free, so the construction has no power to exclude the physically-relevant 'opposite worlds.'
